title: Delirium: Fog, Grand Mirror, Simulacrum and Tangmazu
summary: How Delirium works in Path of Exile 2 after the 0.5 rework: the Mirror and fog, pushing deeper, the Grand Mirror, Delirious Effect, the current Simulacrum, Distilled Emotions and the Tangmazu gate.
description: A reference for the Delirium end-game system in Path of Exile 2: starting a Mirror, fog direction and depth, the continue-or-exit call, the Grand Mirror route, Delirious Effect, Simulacrum access and waves, Distilled Emotions and the Tangmazu path.
prerequisites: Maps unlocked and you can sustain Waystones
A character that survives buffed monsters
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: Omniphobia, Fear Manifest, the Simulacrum boss of Path of Exile 2

items.title: What starts a Delirium?
body: A Delirium Mirror appears in a map. Walking into it spreads fog across the area; monsters inside the fog are buffed and drop better loot.
The deeper you push into the fog, the higher the rewards and the tougher the monsters.

items.title: What is the Grand Mirror?
body: The Grand Mirror is the larger Delirium encounter. It spreads fog more widely and is the step that builds the Delirious Effect on your map.

items.title: How do I reach the Simulacrum?
body: Completing Delirium content generates the Simulacrum. The current 0.5 Simulacrum runs its own wave layout and ends in a boss; it is not the old 15-wave format.

items.title: What are Distilled Emotions for?
body: Distilled Emotions are Delirium currency with two uses: upgrading a map to Delirious, and anointing an amulet with a passive-tree notable.

sections.title: Mirror and fog basics
paragraphs: A Delirium Mirror is the entry point. Touching it wakes the fog, which then creeps outward from the mirror.
Monsters caught in the fog are empowered and yield richer rewards, so the encounter is a risk-reward push rather than a clean clear.
The fog has a fixed origin at the mirror; everything you kill inside it counts toward the Delirium reward, not just the mirror itself.
bullets: Kill inside the fog for rewards

sections.title: Fog direction and depth
paragraphs: Fog spreads outward from the mirror. Plan your path so you chase the fog edge instead of backtracking through cleared ground.
Depth matters: the further the fog has spread and the longer you stay in it, the stronger monsters get and the better the drops.
If the fog is about to overtake a chokepoint you cannot clear, that is your signal to exit rather than die inside it.

sections.title: Continue or exit?
sections.intro: Decide on monster pressure, not greed.

rows.risk: Keep what the fog already granted
rows.when: Your screen is overwhelmed or damage is spiking
You are clearing comfortably and rewards are climbing
Only with a geared, buffed-monster-proof character

sections.title: Grand Mirror route
paragraphs: The Grand Mirror is the wider Delirium encounter on the Atlas. Entering it spreads fog across a much larger area than a normal mirror.
Clearing Grand Mirror content stacks the Delirious Effect on the map, which is what eventually generates the Simulacrum.
Treat the Grand Mirror as a commitment: it assumes you can handle heavily buffed monsters for the whole spread, not just a corner of the map.
bullets: Wider fog than a normal mirror

sections.caption: How Delirious Effect scales as fog deepens. Relative, not exact numbers.

sections.title: Simulacrum access
paragraphs: The Simulacrum is generated by building Delirious Effect through Delirium content. Once enough effect accrues, the Simulacrum becomes available.
The current 0.5 Simulacrum is its own encounter with a wave layout that ends in a boss; do not follow old 15-wave footage, which no longer matches.
Simulacrum Splinters feed the Simulacrum economy; confirm the current combine and entry method on the live item, since it has changed across versions.
bullets: Current waves end in a boss

sections.caption: Conceptual wave shape of the current Simulacrum. Exact count confirmed in-client.

sections.title: Distilled Emotions
paragraphs: Distilled Emotions drop from Delirium content. They have two distinct uses, so decide before spending.
Use one to upgrade a map into a Delirious map for more Delirium reward, or use them to anoint an amulet with a passive-tree notable.
Do not mix the two uses casually: anointing consumes them permanently on the amulet, while map upgrades are a repeatable sink.

sections.title: Reaching Tangmazu
paragraphs: Tangmazu is the boss reached after completing the Simulacrum. The Simulacrum is the gate that opens the Tangmazu path.
Tangmazu assumes a character that already cleared the Simulacrum boss, so do not attempt it under-geared.
This guide covers the path and preparation; the boss page covers Tangmazu's attacks in detail once reachable.

sections.intro: Community experiences; treat as strategy, not guaranteed math.

cards.title: Chase the fog edge
body: Players consistently report that pathing along the fog edge yields far more rewards than clearing dead ground.

cards.title: Exit before overwhelm
body: Most deaths happen one band past a safe exit; leaving early keeps the haul.

cards.title: Old videos mislead
body: The 15-wave footage still floating around does not match the current Simulacrum.

sections.title: Common problems
paragraphs: If the fog ends your run with almost nothing, you likely stayed in cleared ground; chase the fog edge next time.
If the Simulacrum never appears, you have not built enough Delirious Effect; push deeper fog and the Grand Mirror.
If a guide shows 15 waves, it is pre-0.5 and does not match the current Simulacrum; follow the current layout.
